Given:
- Solid: Pentagonal prism
- Base edge = $30\text{ mm}$, Axis length = $60\text{ mm}$
- Condition 1: Rests on an edge of its base in the H.P.
- Condition 2: Axis is parallel to V.P.
- Condition 3: Axis is inclined at $45^\circ$ to the H.P.

### **Steps of Construction:**
1. **Stage 1 (Initial Position):**
   - Assume the prism rests on one of its base edges on the H.P. such that the base is perpendicular to H.P. and parallel to V.P. (or draw base with an edge perpendicular to the reference line in top view).
   - Draw the top view as a regular pentagon with an edge perpendicular to the $XY$ line.
   - Project the front view as a rectangle of size $30\text{ mm}$ (base width) $\times 60\text{ mm}$ (axis length) resting on the $XY$ line.

2. **Stage 2 (Inclined Position):**
   - Tilt the front view rectangle such that its axis makes an angle of $45^\circ$ with the $XY$ line, while keeping the resting edge point fixed on the $XY$ line.
   - Project the top view downwards from the tilted front view and horizontally from the initial top view to obtain the final top view.
   - Ensure all visible and hidden edges are appropriately marked with continuous and dashed lines.
proTip: When a solid rests on a base edge, tilt the axis by the given angle in the second stage while keeping the resting edge fixed on HP.
